deepcolor.config.title: Deep Color
deepcolor.config.gradient.tooltip: Near-black ramp with 8-bit, output-depth and dithered strips side by side. Press P there to measure the real output.
deepcolor.config.restart: Output bits and internal format apply after a restart.
deepcolor.option.dither.tooltip: Adds a fine noise just below one brightness step before the image is rounded to the display's bit depth. Removes banding in dark gradients.
deepcolor.option.strength.tooltip: Noise amplitude in brightness steps (LSB). 1.00 removes banding completely. Lower values give less grain but let some banding back in.
deepcolor.option.temporal.tooltip: Changes the noise every frame so your eye averages it out. Least visible at high frame rates. Off gives a fixed, still grain.
deepcolor.option.dither_bits.tooltip: Bit depth the noise is made for. Auto uses 10 bits in exclusive fullscreen and 8 bits otherwise, because with HDR off Windows reduces windowed games to 8 bits.
deepcolor.option.noise_pattern.tooltip: Blue noise puts the grain at the finest scale, where it is least visible. Gradient noise is the older, slightly cheaper pattern.
deepcolor.option.output_bits.tooltip: Bit depth requested from the driver for the window. Auto and 10-bit both ask for 10 bits and fall back if the driver refuses. Needs a restart.
deepcolor.option.internal_format.tooltip: Precision of the game's own render targets. 16-bit float keeps the most detail in dark scenes. 8-bit is vanilla. Needs a restart.
deepcolor.option.hdr_output.tooltip: When Windows HDR is on, the game sets its own brightness in nits instead of using Windows' SDR content brightness slider, and can use the monitor's full range. On macOS it uses the display's EDR headroom, with the Vulkan backend only. Has no effect while HDR is off. Needs a restart.
deepcolor.option.hdr_ui_nits.tooltip: Brightness of white menus and text, and the base level the world is scaled from. 203 nits is the standard for SDR content in HDR. Auto follows the Windows SDR content brightness slider. On macOS, 203 nits means SDR white.
deepcolor.option.hdr_peak_nits.tooltip: Brightest the world may get. Auto uses the peak Windows knows for your monitor, from the Windows HDR Calibration app, or the current EDR headroom on macOS.
deepcolor.option.hdr_mapping.tooltip: How the world uses the range above interface brightness. Highlights lifts bright things like sky, sun and light sources toward the peak and leaves shadows alone. Linear scales the whole world. None keeps the world at interface brightness.
deepcolor.option.hdr_gamma.tooltip: How dark shadows and midtones are. Higher is darker, white stays the same. 2.2 matches a typical monitor in SDR, 2.4 to 2.6 is a dark-room or film look. The lowest position is the sRGB curve Windows uses for SDR apps in HDR mode, which looks washed out. Applies immediately.
deepcolor.option.hdr_shadow_floor.toolti: OLED panels in HDR mode turn very dark levels into pure black, so a dark gradient ends in a hard edge. This lifts only the darkest shadows to this brightness, keeping true black black. Find the value with the near-black pattern on the gradient screen: the dimmest patch you can still see.
deepcolor.option.hdr_gamut.tooltip: sRGB shows the game's colors accurately. Higher values stretch them toward the Gamut target, like a monitor's native-gamut SDR mode does. If HDR looks duller than SDR, this is usually why. Grays and white do not change.
deepcolor.option.hdr_gamut_target.toolti: The wide gamut that Gamut stretch moves colors toward. Display P3 is close to a QD-OLED's native gamut and the closest match for most SDR modes. Adobe RGB widens greens and cyans. BT.2020 is the widest; the AW2725DF covers about 82% of it, so the most saturated colors get clipped by the panel.
deepcolor.gradient.help: 0: all strips   1-4: one strip   5: grey steps   P: measure   Esc: close
deepcolor.gradient.steps: Grey steps (8-bit shades), identical in SDR and HDR. Photograph both with the same camera settings.
deepcolor.gradient.hdr0: Near-black ramp in nits, black at the far left
deepcolor.gradient.hdr1: Same ramp with shadow floor %s nits
deepcolor.gradient.hdr2: Patches (nits): the dimmest one you can see is your panel's floor
deepcolor.gradient.hdr3: Game shadows, RGB 0 to 32, at the current settings
deepcolor.gradient.hdr_help: HDR near-black test. Set Shadow floor to about the dimmest visible patch. 5: grey steps
